relevance_note: Case report of a neonate with 'a heterozygous 5.15 Mb deletion in 6q23.3q24.3' that affected TNFAIP3, plus a literature table (Table 1) of 11 previously reported patients with 6q deletions involving TNFAIP3.
method_note: Read the full paper by hand. Patient 1 is the first-hand case (the neonate of the Clinical report, the 'Current report' column of Table 1); Patients 2-12 are previously published cases from Table 1 (patients as columns; column headers 'Patient 1' to 'Patient 12' in the second header row, author group in the first header row). A Python script transcribed Table 1 cell by cell and built the JSON; I checked its transcription against the table (counts reproduce the text: 8 female, 5 de novo, 7 with fever as initial symptom). Decisions: (a) '-' cells treated as not reported per rule 6, so no 'excluded' rows from Table 1 although the table separates '-' from 'Not mentioned'; 'unknown' ethnicity/inheritance treated as not reported. (b) First header row has blank cells after 'Endo et al.', 'Tsuchida et al.' and 'Wu et al.'; read as merged headers, so Patients 3, 8 and 12 were assigned to those groups (consistent with 11 patients from 8 references [13-20]) - inferred, please verify. (c) Table 1 lists 'de novo' for Patients 1, 4, 5, 6, 11 but no parental testing is described, so inheritance = not reported under rule 8 (Table text kept in parental_testing_statement); 'paternal'/'maternal' recorded as stated. (d) Table 'Fever' and initial-symptom 'Infections'/'Respiratory- infections' for literature patients were not mapped to checklist 'recurrent fever'/'recurrent infections' (broader terms; recurrence not stated per patient). (e) Initial-symptom cells are concatenated in the Markdown (e.g. 'FeverRespiratory- infectionsGastroenteritis'); split by reading. 'HLH' in the Anemia row (Patient 5) recorded as feature 'HLH', not as anemia. Henoch-Schonlein purpura (Patient 9) mapped to checklist vasculitis and skin lesions; Rosacea (Patient 10) to skin lesions; Gastroenteritis (Patient 4) to GI inflammation. (f) Pathogenicity 'pathogenic' for all 12 deletions is from the Fig. 2 legend ('pathogenic deletions') plus the statement that all 12 patients are summarized in Table 1 and Fig. 2. (g) Patient 1 last evaluation taken as the six-month visit (follow-up then suspended). Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: deletion band '6q23.3q24.3' in the text vs '6q23.2q24.3 region' in the Fig. 1 legend; abdominal ultrasonography 'no other abnormalitis except for hepatomegaly' vs splenomegaly on physical examination and Table 1 (splenomegaly kept observed, no excluded row); TORCH including Cytomegalovirus 'normal' vs CMV DNA detected by mNGS and PCR (no excluded CMV row emitted); fever 'resolved gradually within 24 days' vs CRP normal 'accompanied by extinguished fever within 22 days'; text says nine patients had onset 'before the age of 1 year', but Table 1 shows 7 with onset under 1 year and 2 at exactly '1 year'. n_patients_reported = 12 (1 first-hand + 11 from literature). AIHA exclusion for Patient 1 (Discussion) does not exclude the broader 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' item.
